questions.q: A stock trades at $95 at expiration. What is the payoff of a call option with strike K = $100?
questions.explain: Call payoff is max(S - K, 0) = max(95 - 100, 0) = max(-5, 0) = 0. The call is out-of-the-money, so it expires worthless.

questions.q: You buy a put option with strike K = $50 for a premium of $3. At expiration the stock is at $40. What is your profit?
questions.explain: Put payoff is max(K - S, 0) = max(50 - 40, 0) = 10. Profit is payoff minus premium paid: 10 - 3 = 7.

questions.q: What is the key structural difference between a forward contract and an option?
options: Forwards can only be written on stocks; options can be written on anything
A forward obligates both sides to transact; an option gives the buyer a right the seller must honor only if exercised
Options have no expiration date, but forwards do
There is no structural difference; the terms are interchangeable
questions.explain: A forward is a symmetric obligation for both parties. An option is one-sided: the buyer pays a premium for the right to exercise, and the seller is obligated only if the buyer chooses to exercise.

questions.q: A call option has a strike of $80, the stock trades at $92, and the premium is $15. What is the time value of this option?
questions.explain: Intrinsic value = max(S - K, 0) = max(92 - 80, 0) = 12. Time value = premium - intrinsic value = 15 - 12 = 3.

questions.q: Why is a long option position's maximum loss capped at the premium paid, while a long forward position's loss is not capped?
options: Because options are always cheaper than forwards
Because option payoffs can never go below zero, so the worst case is losing the entire premium with no further obligation
Because exchanges guarantee a minimum payoff on all options
Because forwards do not have a strike price
questions.explain: max(S-K, 0) and max(K-S, 0) are both bounded below by zero, so a long option buyer can never owe more than the premium already paid. A forward has no such floor — losses can grow without limit as the underlying moves against the position.
